points.description: States the similarities between iteration and recursion: both involve repetition, both have termination tests/conditions, and both can go on infinitely (infinite loop / infinite recursion). Any wording; the central idea is that they share repetition and a stopping condition (and can fail to stop).
points.partial_credit: Award about 2 marks for one correct similarity, 3-4 marks for two correct similarities, or for three stated vaguely; 5 for all three or for two clearly stated plus a reasonable third.

rubric.notes: Full marks for naming the shared features (repetition, termination test, possible infinite execution) in any wording, however brief or informal. Part marks if only one or two of these are given, scaled generously. Give no marks for only describing differences or defining the terms without any shared feature; extra wrong remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict a similarity.
